title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operating in fully autonomous mode struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas, while a human safety operator was present in the vehicle. The system did not slow down or stop in response to the animal, showing a failure to detect or react to an obstacle in its path. It is not established whether the vehicle's sensors identified the duck, whether the safety operator attempted intervention, or what object-detection thresholds were in place for small animals.

The incident reveals a gap between real-world conditions and the scenarios the system was built to handle. Autonomous vehicles are typically trained on large obstacles like cars and pedestrians, not small animals crossing streets. A human safety operator present in the vehicle did not prevent the collision, indicating either that the operator did not perceive the threat in time or that intervention was not attempted. Whether the company's restriction of testing to certain streets and its simulation experiments will address detection of small animals is not yet established.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping afterward. The incident gained wider attention after a resident posted about it on a neighborhood Facebook group, noting the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign. The duck was well-known locally as it had been nesting in a pot outside an Italian restaurant, and residents have since collected its eggs and placed them in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode during the incident. The company disputes the resident's claim about the stop sign, stating the vehicle made complete and appropriate stops at all relevant intersections after reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scene multiple times. In response, Avride has restricted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around Mueller Lake. The company is now conducting controlled simulation experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations, while ensuring changes do not compromise safety performance. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, also operate in Austin.
